title: First bands in New Orleans: Duck Ernest and Jack Carey
summary: Miller recalls his boyhood friend who played alto and then lists Duck Ernest and Jack Carey as his first bands, with Carey for dance music.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I was raised with him. What was he? What did he play? He played alto. We was in the army together and I learned bugle and I learned bugle. And did he play in any bands? Well he played in any band we had out there in the country, you know, brass bands.
He didn't come here to the city? No. I just wondered, you'd mentioned his name before. Yeah. Tape. You know that kind of thing. Who did you play with first when you came here you say?

Ernest Johnson, but everybody called him Duck Ernest. And then who did you play with? Jack Kerr. And then who? Then before I decided to get my own band. But all the things with Jack come right with me, see. All of them.
Well did you play with two bands at once, have them? Like you'd be with Jack Kerr and then play with?
No. Somebody else at the same time? Oh well if Jack wouldn't have a job then somebody hired I'd go play with them.
And the same with Duck, huh? Yeah. Who were some of the other bands that you used to be with?
Well the other bands I didn't do anything but play parades and you know funerals and things with them. But I played all the dance music with Jack Kerr.
